meta.description: Food truck ordering systems compared: pre-orders with a pickup time, kitchen capacity, schedules, fees and contracts — checked on each vendor’s site.

fit.oursBody: you trade at changing locations, want pre-orders with a pickup time, don’t want your kitchen overloaded, and don’t want a contract.
fit.marketplacesBody: Delivery platforms bring new customers but take commission on every order. Uber Eats states 14% for pickup and 30% for delivery by Uber couriers in Germany. Wolt says on its own website that it charges commission but gives no rates. We could not check Lieferando’s rates. That commission applies to regulars who pre-order with you, too.

faq.whatA: An ordering system takes orders online before customers reach the truck: they choose dishes and a pickup time, pay online or at pickup, and the order appears in your kitchen. A till or card machine takes payment at the truck. The two complement each other.
faq.capacityA: Customers only see pickup times your kitchen can actually make. The system works from each dish’s preparation time and how many you prepare at once.

preorder.label: Pre-orders with a chosen pickup time
preorder.explain: Customers order in advance and choose the time they pick up.

capacity.label: Pickup times limited by kitchen capacity
capacity.explain: Customers only see pickup times the kitchen can actually make.

asap.explain: Customers can order without choosing a time and pick up as soon as it is ready.

payattruck.explain: Customers order online and pay when they pick up.
